# Faber

> Faber is a statically typed compute language designed for coding agents and
> human authors: one semantic program, rendered in the reader's locale and
> lowered to the target you need from a single high-level intermediate
> representation (HIR).

## Identity

- Language: Faber. License: MIT.
- Compiler: Radix — closed-source while in development; ships inside the `faber` CLI.
- Status: v1 series experimental; device GPU inference is not shipped.
- This repository (`faberlang/faber`): language home — grammar, target support matrices, target API packages, docs.
- Releases: https://github.com/faberlang/releases/releases

## Entry points

- This file — https://github.com/faberlang/faber/blob/main/llms.txt
- Agent guide — https://faberlang.dev/agents/index.md
- Documentation site machine index — https://faberlang.dev/llms.txt
- Agent skills catalog — https://faberlang.dev/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json
- Human documentation — https://faberlang.dev/en-US/

## Repositories

- faberlang/faber — this repository: language home, target APIs, grammar
- faberlang/gradus — open autograd/ML library written in Faber
- faberlang/norma — standard library source
- faberlang/cista — package store and lock writer
- faberlang/hosts — concrete host implementations
- faberlang/examples — examples and application packages
- faberlang/faberlang.dev — documentation site
- faberlang/releases — signed release archives and checksums

## Language facts

- Declarations are type-first: `int a`, never `a: int`.
- Runtime assignment uses `←`; `=` is a compile-time fact only.
- Nullability is an explicit union: `T ∪ null`.
- Tensor operators are glyphs: `·` matrix multiplication, `⊗` outer product, `⊙` Hadamard product.
- Output is the line-level `print` statement, not a function call.
- Comments are `#` on their own line.
- English is the default authoring locale; the same program renders in Latin,
  Arabic, Hindi, Vietnamese, Thai, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese.
- Formal grammar: https://github.com/faberlang/faber/blob/main/docs/EBNF.md

## What not to assume

- No public Radix source checkout — the compiler is closed-source while in development.
- Device GPU inference is not shipped — bounded dual-backend training on Metal and CUDA is the proven device claim.
- The v1 surface is experimental — treat it as under active development, not stable.
